h1: The 7 Best Gas Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Gas Leaf Blowers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven gas leaf blowers from Echo, Husqvarna, PROYAMA, HASANEN and SENIX, compared on airflow, carry style and price.
summary: The Echo 79.9 cc X Series backpack blower tops the list on airflow, at 1110 CFM, for buyers who will spend over $500. The Husqvarna 150BT is the balanced backpack pick at 765 CFM, and the PROYAMA 72CC is the value backpack at 880 CFM. For small yards, the SENIX 4-cycle handheld is the cheap way in.
intro: Gas blowers look simple until you notice that the CFM figure does not tell you how the machine feels at the end of an hour. Carry style, handheld versus backpack, matters as much as raw airflow once your yard gets past a quarter acre.

We reviewed seven gas models and ranked them on listed airflow, carry format, engine detail and price band. Two models are handheld and five are backpack. Their prices run from the $50 to $100 range up past $500.

products.name: Echo 220 MPH 1110 CFM 79.9 cc Gas 2-Stroke X Series Backpack Blower
products.verdict: The highest airflow and air speed in the group, in a backpack.
products.description:
The Echo X Series is a 79.9 cc 2-stroke gas backpack blower rated at 1110 CFM and 220 MPH, priced above $500.

Nothing else here lists both a figure over 1000 CFM and an air speed. It outguns the PB-770T under it by roughly 350 CFM on paper, and that gap is the justification for the cost.

Choose it for large properties and heavy debris. The caveat is the price, which only makes sense if you use it often.

products.name: PB-770T - Echo Backpack Blower - Commercial Grade 63.3 cc
products.verdict: A commercial-grade 63.3 cc backpack at 756 CFM.
products.description:
The Echo PB-770T is a commercial-grade 63.3 cc backpack blower with 756 CFM listed, priced above $500.

The smaller engine and lower airflow are what separate it from the X Series above, and it asks the same top-tier price. Its draw is the commercial-grade description rather than raw numbers.

It suits buyers who value the grade and brand. The caveat is that 756 CFM is similar to cheaper backpack models below.
products.idealFor: Pros who want a commercial-grade label.
products.skipIf: You want the most CFM per dollar.

products.name: Husqvarna 150BT Gas Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 765 CFM backpack from a major brand under $500.
products.description:
The Husqvarna 150BT is a gas backpack blower listed at 765 CFM, priced between $200 and $500.

It costs well under the two Echo models and lists a bit more airflow than the PB-770T. Against the budget backpacks below, the brand is what you pay for.

It suits homeowners with a large yard. The caveat is that the listing gives no engine size.

products.name: PROYAMA 72CC Gas Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 72 cc backpack listed at 880 CFM for $100 to $200.
products.description:
The PROYAMA is a 72 cc gas backpack blower with 880 CFM listed, in the $100 to $200 range.

On paper it out-blows the Husqvarna 150BT for far less. The tradeoff is brand reputation and the thinner track record that goes with a lesser-known name.

It suits value hunters with a big yard. The caveat is that the brand is less established than Echo or Husqvarna.

products.name: HASANEN Backpack Gas Powered Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The cheapest backpack here, with 850 CFM listed.
products.description:
The HASANEN is a gas backpack blower listed at 850 CFM, in the $50 to $100 range.

It undercuts every other backpack on price while listing airflow close to the PROYAMA. What you give up is brand depth and any detail about the engine.

It suits buyers who want the lowest-cost backpack. The caveat is thin listing detail.

products.name: Husqvarna 125B Gas Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A handheld gas blower at 470 CFM from a major brand.
products.description:
The Husqvarna 125B is a handheld gas blower rated at 470 CFM, in the $200 to $500 range.

It trades the backpack airflow of the models above for a lighter carry. The price is the sticking point, since the cheaper backpacks list nearly double the CFM.

It suits mid-size yards where you want less weight. The caveat is that it is the priciest handheld here.

products.name: SENIX 4QL 26.5cc 4-Cycle Handheld Gas Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 26.5 cc 4-cycle handheld for small yards.
products.description:
The SENIX 4QL is a 26.5 cc 4-cycle handheld gas blower rated at 410 CFM, in the $50 to $100 range.

It has the lowest airflow in the group, but the 4-cycle engine means you do not mix oil into the fuel. That is the practical reason to consider it.

It suits small yards and quick jobs. The caveat is that 410 CFM is modest for big areas.

whatMatters.detail: CFM is the volume of air moved each minute. More clears bigger piles faster. Look for the figure in the title.
A backpack puts weight on your shoulders and hips, which suits long sessions. A handheld is lighter to grab. Check the carry style in the listing.
A 2-stroke engine runs on mixed fuel, while a 4-cycle runs on plain gas with separate oil. The SENIX lists 4-cycle. Check which your model uses.
Engine size in cc roughly signals power class. The Echo X Series lists 79.9 cc and the PROYAMA 72 cc. Compare the cc in the title.
MPH shows how hard the air hits debris. Only the Echo X Series lists it here, at 220 MPH. Check for it if you clear wet leaves.

faq.q: Do gas blowers need mixed fuel?
faq.a: 2-stroke models, like the Echo X Series, run on mixed fuel. The SENIX is a 4-cycle, which the listing says avoids mixing.
Buying a handheld for a large yard. The backpacks list far more airflow.

faq.q: Is the Echo worth it over the PROYAMA?
faq.a: Only for frequent heavy use. The PROYAMA lists 880 CFM for far less.
Follow the owner manual. The listings do not detail the starting process.

faq.q: How do I maintain a gas blower?
faq.a: Use fresh fuel and follow the maker's care guide. The listings do not give maintenance steps.
The listings do not say. Lesser-known brands carry less track record than Echo or Husqvarna.

finalTake: The Echo X Series is the best gas leaf blower for demanding jobs, and the Husqvarna 150BT is the balanced pick under $500. The PROYAMA gives the most airflow for the money, and the SENIX handles small yards. Pick the carry style before the CFM.
